books.title: More Baby Animals
books.art_why: Real baby animals and their mothers exist today and photograph beautifully.

pages.text: Do you know what baby animals are called?
pages.brief: A bright green meadow where several very young animals stand close together on soft grass, a small fluffy one, a tiny brown one and a small grey one, all facing forward with a few white wildflowers around their feet.

pages.text: A baby deer is called a fawn.
pages.brief: A spotted fawn stands on long thin legs beside its mother deer in a sunlit forest clearing. The fawn's white spots show clearly on its soft brown coat. Ferns and tall grass surround them, with dappled light falling through the trees.

pages.text: A baby donkey is called a foal.
pages.brief: A young foal stands close to its mother donkey in a dry grassy field. The foal has long ears, a soft grey-brown coat and thin wobbly legs. A wooden fence and a few low bushes sit behind them under a clear blue sky.

pages.text: A baby gorilla is called an infant.
pages.brief: A small black-haired infant gorilla clings to its mother's chest in dense green jungle. The mother gorilla sits among leafy plants with one big arm curled around her baby. Thick leaves and branches fill the background behind them.

pages.text: A baby pig is called a piglet.
pages.brief: A pink piglet trots beside its mother pig in a farmyard pen, curly tail up and small pointed ears forward. Its snout is close to the muddy ground. Straw and a low wooden fence are behind them.

pages.text: A baby koala is called a joey.
pages.brief: A tiny koala joey clings to its mother's back high in a eucalyptus tree. The mother koala grips the branch with strong claws while the joey peeks over her shoulder. Green leaves surround them against a pale sky.

pages.text: A baby owl is called an owlet.
pages.brief: A fluffy owlet sits in a twig nest beside its mother owl, high in a tree. The owlet's big round eyes look straight ahead and its soft downy feathers fluff out. Leaves and branches surround the nest.

pages.text: Which other baby animals do you know?
pages.brief: Several different baby animals stand together in a green meadow, a small fluffy one, a spotted one and a tiny grey one, with soft grass and a few wildflowers around their feet under open sky.

books.title: Apple Tree
books.art_why: Apple trees and seeds exist in the real world today, so photographs suit this nature cycle.

pages.text: An apple grows in a cycle. How does the cycle go?
pages.brief: A ripe red apple hangs from a leafy branch in a simple outdoor garden, with soft curving shapes around it that suggest a repeating cycle. The apple is shown whole and clear, and the setting stays plain so the fruit is the focus.

pages.text: First comes the seed.
pages.brief: A single apple seed rests on dark soil in a garden bed, shown close and clear. The small brown seed lies alone with loose earth around it, ready to begin. The scene is simple and outdoors, with no other plants or creatures.

pages.text: Then comes the sprout.
pages.brief: A tiny green sprout pushes up from dark soil, with two small leaves opening at the top. It stands alone in the garden bed, lit by soft daylight. Loose earth surrounds its thin stem, and no other plants are nearby.

pages.text: Next come the years.
pages.brief: A simple outdoor garden bed sits under a wide sky as soft bands of light and shadow move across the dark soil, suggesting long stretches of time. The empty bed remains in the same spot, with loose earth and no plants yet.

pages.text: Then comes the tree.
pages.brief: A full-grown apple tree stands in an open garden, with a thick brown trunk and a wide canopy of green leaves. Its branches spread out under a bright sky, and the tree is shown alone in the same outdoor spot.

pages.text: Next come the blooms.
pages.brief: Pink and white apple blossoms open along the branches of the apple tree. The tree is covered in many small flowers, with soft petals visible against green leaves. The blossoms are the focus in the open garden under a bright sky.

pages.text: Then come the apples.
pages.brief: Ripe red apples hang from the branches of the apple tree among green leaves. Several apples are visible, round and bright, growing in the open garden. The tree fills the scene under a clear sky, with the fruit as the main focus.

pages.text: Seeds wait inside each apple. The cycle begins again.
pages.brief: A ripe red apple lies open on dark soil, showing the small brown seeds tucked inside its core. The seeds are clearly visible in the centre of the fruit, and the apple rests in a simple outdoor garden bed.

books.title: Animal Costumes
books.art_why: Real animals wearing real costumes can be photographed today.

pages.text: People wear costumes. Animals can wear costumes too.
pages.brief: Two children stand dressed up in colourful costumes, one in a cape and one in a tall hat, beside a small group of animals that are also wearing simple costumes, all of them posed together and facing the reader on a plain bright background.

pages.text: A dog can wear wings.
pages.brief: A dog stands squarely facing the reader wearing a pair of wings strapped to its back, the wings spread out to either side of its body, the dog's head up and ears forward, photographed against a plain light background so the wings stand out clearly.

pages.text: A dog can wear a mane.
pages.brief: A dog sits facing the reader wearing a thick mane around its neck and head, the shaggy fur of the mane framing its face, the dog calm and still with its mouth slightly open, shown against a plain background so the mane is easy to see.

pages.text: A goat can wear a crown.
pages.brief: A goat stands facing the reader wearing a small crown set on top of its head between its horns, the goat's beard hanging down and its ears out to the sides, photographed against a plain light background so the crown shows clearly.

pages.text: A cat can wear a bandanna.
pages.brief: A cat sits facing the reader wearing a bandanna tied around its neck, the cloth hanging in a triangle over its chest, the cat upright with its tail curled beside it, shown against a plain background so the bandanna is clearly visible.

pages.text: A dog can wear a mask.
pages.brief: A dog stands facing the reader wearing a mask over the upper part of its face, the mask shaped around its eyes and nose, the dog's ears up and its body still, photographed against a plain light background so the mask stands out clearly.

pages.text: A dog can wear fins.
pages.brief: A dog stands facing the reader wearing fins fitted onto its legs and sides, the fins flat and angled outward like a swimmer's, the dog steady on its feet, shown against a plain background so every fin is easy to see.

pages.text: A rabbit can wear a hat.
pages.brief: A rabbit sits upright facing the reader wearing a hat balanced on its head between its long ears, the hat sitting straight, the rabbit's front paws tucked in and its whiskers forward, photographed against a plain light background.

pages.text: A dog can wear a snout.
pages.brief: A dog stands facing the reader wearing a snout fitted over its own nose and muzzle, the false snout pushing forward from its face, the dog's ears up and its body still, shown against a plain background so the snout is clearly visible.

pages.text: What is this dog wearing?
pages.brief: A dog stands facing the reader wearing a full costume that covers it from head to body, the outfit clearly visible all over, the dog still and its ears up, photographed against a plain light background so the reader can look closely and name what it has on.

books.title: What Season Is It?
books.art_why: Seasons, leaves, snow and flowers are real things a camera can capture today.

pages.text: The leaves change color. When do leaves change color?
pages.brief: A close view of a leafy tree branch where the leaves have turned yellow, orange and red, some still clinging to the twigs while a few have drifted down onto the ground below. Soft outdoor daylight shows the changing colors clearly across the whole branch.

pages.text: Leaves change color in fall.
pages.brief: A park path in fall with trees whose leaves are now deep red, orange and brown. Fallen leaves lie scattered and thick on the ground around the trunks, and more leaves are drifting down through the air, settling on the path and the grass beside it.

pages.text: The snow falls. When does snow fall?
pages.brief: Thick white snow falling steadily from a pale grey sky over a quiet open field. Flakes are visible in the air close to the viewer, and a thin layer of snow is already gathering on the ground and on the bare branches of a small bush nearby.

pages.text: Snow falls in winter.
pages.brief: A winter scene under falling snow, with a wide field and bare trees all coated in white. Snowflakes drift down through the cold air, the ground is covered in a fresh white layer, and the light is soft and grey across the whole quiet landscape.

pages.text: The flowers grow. When do flowers grow?
pages.brief: Small green flower shoots pushing up out of dark soil, with tight buds opening into the first bright petals. A few more shoots are just breaking through the earth nearby, and soft spring daylight falls across the soil and the young plants.

pages.text: Flowers grow in spring.
pages.brief: A spring garden bed filled with blooming flowers in yellow, pink and white, their stems and green leaves fresh and new. More buds are opening around them, the soil is dark and damp, and gentle daylight shows the flowers standing upright and growing.

pages.text: The days become hot. When do days become hot?
pages.brief: A bright, glaring sun high in a clear blue sky over a dry open field. The ground looks warm and dusty, the air shimmers slightly, and there is no shade in sight, showing a very hot day in the open.

pages.text: Days become hot in summer.
pages.brief: A hot summer day in an open field under a strong bright sun and a deep blue sky. The grass looks dry and sunlit, the light is harsh and bright across the ground, and the whole scene shows the long, warm hours of summer.

books.title: City Shapes
books.art_why: City streets and buildings exist in real life today.

pages.text: Look around the city. What shapes do you see?
pages.brief: A bright city street is shown from eye level, with tall buildings on both sides, sidewalks, streetlights, and open sky overhead. The wide view invites a careful look around at the shapes all over the city.

pages.text: Here you see an oval.
pages.brief: A large oval shape appears in the middle of a city scene, with a building wall and smooth sidewalk nearby. The oval is clear and easy to see, standing out against the simple city background.

pages.text: Here you see triangles.
pages.brief: Several triangle shapes appear around a city street, with building fronts and pavement nearby. The triangles are clear and easy to spot, set against a simple city background with open space around them. They stand out clearly in the scene.

pages.text: Here you see a circle.
pages.brief: A large circle shape appears in a city setting, with a building wall and sidewalk close by. The circle is clear and easy to spot, standing out against the simple city background around it. The scene is bright.

pages.text: Here you see squares.
pages.brief: Square shapes appear in a city scene, with building fronts and pavement nearby. The squares are clear and easy to spot, standing out against the simple city background. The scene is bright and open around them.

pages.text: Here you see rectangles.
pages.brief: Rectangle shapes appear in a city scene, with building fronts and street pavement nearby. The rectangles are clear and easy to spot, standing out against the simple city background around them. The view is bright and open.

pages.text: Here you see hexagons.
pages.brief: Hexagon shapes appear in a city scene, with building walls and sidewalk nearby. The hexagons are clear and easy to spot, standing out against the simple city background around them. The view is bright and open.

pages.text: Here you see many shapes. What shapes do you see?
pages.brief: A city street scene shows many shapes together, including ovals, triangles, circles, squares, rectangles, and hexagons among buildings and sidewalks. The shapes are clear and easy to spot around them in the bright, open city view.

books.title: Snow Falls
books.art_why: Snow, mountains, plains, forest, ocean and desert are real places that exist today.

pages.text: Snow falls in the mountains.
pages.brief: Wide view of tall mountain peaks under a pale sky, with snowflakes drifting down steadily over the rock and high slopes. The mountains stand quiet and cold, filling the frame from a distance, and the falling snow softens their edges as it lands.

pages.text: Snow falls on the plains.
pages.brief: Open flat plains stretch far to the horizon under a grey sky, and snow falls across the wide grassland. Nothing blocks the view in any direction, and the flakes come down steadily over the low, even land, dusting the ground as they settle.

pages.text: Snow falls in the forest.
pages.brief: A forest of tall trees stands close together, branches reaching up while snow falls through them. Flakes drift down between the trunks and settle on the branches and forest floor, and the whole woodland is quiet under the steady falling snow.

pages.text: Snow falls on the ocean.
pages.brief: Snow falls over the open ocean, flakes coming down onto the wide water and the small waves. The sea reaches out to the horizon under a cold sky, and the snow drifts down over the surface of the water without stopping.

pages.text: Snow falls in the desert.
pages.brief: Snow falls over a desert of sand dunes, flakes drifting down onto the dry, rippled sand. The dunes roll away under a pale sky, and the snow keeps coming, settling lightly on the bare slopes where nothing grows.

pages.text: Snow falls in the winter.
pages.brief: A winter scene shows snow falling steadily over a cold landscape. The ground is white and the sky is grey, and flakes come down through the chilly air, covering everything in a soft, even layer of winter snow.

pages.text: Snow falls in the spring.
pages.brief: Snow falls in springtime, flakes drifting down through the air over the landscape in the spring season. The snow keeps coming down, landing on the ground below, even as the season has turned to spring.

pages.text: Snow falls from the clouds. We fall in the snow!
pages.brief: Clouds fill the sky above, and snow falls from them down toward the ground. Below, children play in the deep snow, tumbling and falling into it with arms out, landing in the soft white drifts as the flakes keep coming down.

books.title: Wash Your Hands
books.art_why: Real children, sinks and everyday hygiene are things a camera can photograph today.

pages.text: Wash your hands before you eat.
pages.brief: A young child stands at a bathroom sink, rubbing soapy hands together under running water, sleeves pushed up. Behind the open door a small table is set with a plate of food and a cup, waiting for the meal to begin. Bright bathroom light, towel on a rail nearby.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you sneeze.
pages.brief: A child with a tissue at the nose, mid-sneeze, standing in a cozy living room. The same child then leans over a bathroom sink, washing both hands with soap and water, a soap dispenser and folded towel on the counter beside them.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you use the bathroom.
pages.brief: A small child in a bathroom, standing at the sink turning the tap, soap in one hand. A toilet is visible behind them in the clean tiled room. Water runs over their fingers as they wash, a towel hanging ready on the wall.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you dig.
pages.brief: A child kneeling in a garden, hands covered in dark soil, a small trowel and a leafy plant beside them. Next, at an outdoor tap or bathroom sink, the child rinses muddy hands under running water, dirt washing away into the basin.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you paint.
pages.brief: A child at a low table with pots of bright paint and a brush, fingers smeared with red and blue. Then the child stands at a sink, scrubbing painted hands with soap, colourful smudges fading under the running water, paper paintings drying nearby.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you pet a dog.
pages.brief: A child crouches on a floor beside a friendly dog, one hand stroking its back. Afterwards the child stands at a bathroom sink, washing hands with soap under the tap, the dog sitting and watching from the doorway.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you play.
pages.brief: A child playing outdoors on a sunny day, running with a ball, hands dusty from the ground. Then inside at the sink, the child washes both hands under running water, soap bubbles on the fingers, a towel on the counter.

pages.text: Wash front and back. Wash between your fingers, too!
pages.brief: Close view of a child's hands at a sink, palms turned up and then turned over, rubbing soap across the backs and fronts. The fingers are interlaced, lather between them, running water and a soap dish beside the basin.

books.title: Circles
books.art_why: Circles in nature and everyday life are real, photographable subjects.

pages.text: Circles are around the Sun.
pages.brief: A bright Sun shines in space, and clear circles surround it. The circles ring the Sun in a simple pattern, showing the round shapes named on this page. No planets, people or other objects are added; the focus stays on the Sun and the circles around it.

pages.text: Circles are in the middle of flowers.
pages.brief: Close-up flowers open their petals, and each flower has a clear circle in its middle. The round centers sit at the heart of the blooms, showing the circles named on this page. The flowers are the only objects shown, with no people or animals added.

pages.text: Circles are on lily pads in a pond.
pages.brief: Green lily pads float on a pond, and clear circles sit on the pads. The round shapes rest on the flat leaves on the water, showing the circles named on this page. The pond and lily pads are the only setting, with no people or animals added.

pages.text: Circles are on rolls of hay.
pages.brief: Round rolls of hay stand in a field, and their circular ends face the viewer. The circles show clearly on the rolls, matching the round shapes named on this page. The hay rolls are the only objects shown, with no people or animals added.

pages.text: Circles are on a butterfly’s wings.
pages.brief: A butterfly rests with its wings open, and clear circles mark the wings. The round shapes sit on the butterfly’s wings, showing the circles named on this page. The butterfly is the only animal shown, with no other objects or people added.

pages.text: Circles are in tree rings.
pages.brief: A cut tree trunk shows its rings, and the rings form clear circles. The round lines sit inside the trunk, showing the circles named on this page. The tree trunk is the only object shown, with no people, animals or other objects added.

pages.text: Do you see circles here?
pages.brief: Several plain circles are arranged in a clear space for the reader to look at and find. The circles are the only named things shown; no people, animals or other objects appear, and the reader is invited to see the circles here.

books.title: What Groups Do You See?
books.art_why: The book shows real toys and animal figures that can be photographed.

pages.text: The teddy bears are one group.
pages.brief: A row of small soft teddy bears sits close together, clearly gathered as one group. Their different sizes and colours are visible, but they are all shown together as the teddy bears in the scene.

pages.text: What other groups do you see?
pages.brief: The same toy scene is shown with teddy bears and other small toys visible in clusters. The arrangement invites viewers to look again and notice which other toys or animal figures could be gathered together as another group.

pages.text: The tiny animals are one group.
pages.brief: A small cluster of tiny animal figures stands close together as one group. Their little shapes and colours are clear as the tiny animals sit gathered in the same nearby area, making a separate group.

pages.text: What other groups do you see?
pages.brief: The scene shows the tiny animals and other toys arranged in visible clusters. Viewers are invited to look carefully and notice another way the toys or animal figures could be sorted into a new group.

pages.text: The animals on the blue pillow are one group.
pages.brief: Several small animal figures sit together on a soft blue pillow, gathered as one clear group. The blue pillow is clearly visible beneath them, and the small animals are grouped together in that one place.

pages.text: What other groups do you see?
pages.brief: The toys and animal figures are shown again in the scene, with the blue pillow and other groups visible. Viewers can look around and find another group that could be made from the animals and toys on display.

pages.text: Look at these animals. What other groups could you make?
pages.brief: A collection of animal figures is laid out together, ready to be looked at closely. Different ways of grouping the animals are possible, and viewers are invited to think of another group they could make from these animals.

books.title: Swamps
books.art_why: Real swamps and their plants, animals and water can be photographed today.

pages.text: Swamps are areas of wet and dry land.
pages.brief: A broad swamp scene showing shallow wet water and patches of dry grassy land beside it. Reeds and low green plants grow at the water's edge, and the ground rises slightly into drier banks under a soft sky.

pages.text: Swamps can have fresh water.
pages.brief: A freshwater swamp with clear, calm water winding between green plants and mossy trees. Light reflects on the surface, and leafy branches lean over the water, showing a lush wet habitat full of fresh water.

pages.text: Swamps can have salt water.
pages.brief: A saltwater swamp near a coastal shore, with brackish water among tough grasses and tangled roots. The water stretches between muddy banks and low vegetation, showing a swamp where salt water is present.

pages.text: Swamps can have many plants.
pages.brief: A swamp crowded with many plants: tall reeds, broad-leafed plants, moss, ferns and shrubs growing in and around shallow water. Green leaves fill the scene, with stems rising from wet ground and still water.

pages.text: Swamps can have many animals.
pages.brief: A lively swamp showing many animals: a turtle on a log, a frog near the water, a heron standing in shallows, dragonflies above the surface and small fish below. Plants and wet ground surround them.

pages.text: Swamps help the soil stay healthy.
pages.brief: A close view of dark, moist soil among swamp plants and roots. Healthy green plants grow from the rich wet earth, and shallow water lies nearby, showing soil held in place by the swamp's dense roots and vegetation.

pages.text: Swamps help the air stay clean.
pages.brief: An open swamp under a wide clear sky, with green plants and calm water below. Fresh leaves and reeds fill the foreground, and the unclouded air above the wetland looks clean and open.

pages.text: Swamps help the water stay clean.
pages.brief: Clear water in a swamp, with visible plants and roots beneath the surface. The water looks clean and still among green reeds and mossy banks, reflecting light and showing a healthy wetland environment.

pages.text: Swamps help the land stay dry.
pages.brief: A swamp beside higher, drier land. Water spreads through the wetland among reeds and roots, while the nearby grassy bank stands above the waterline, showing wet swamp ground next to dry land.

pages.text: Swamps help Earth stay healthy.
pages.brief: A wide view of a green, healthy swamp with plants, calm water and a few animals, set within a larger natural landscape. The wetland looks lush and balanced, suggesting a healthy Earth with clean water, air and soil.

books.title: Ladybugs
books.art_why: Ladybugs are real animals living today, so photographs can show their colours and patterns accurately.

pages.text: All ladybugs are insects.
pages.brief: A close group of ladybugs shown together, filling the frame, each with a round domed body, a small head with short antennae and six legs. Each one is seen clearly from above so the shared insect body shape is plain.

pages.text: Some ladybugs are red. Some ladybugs are yellow.
pages.brief: Two ladybugs side by side, one with a bright red rounded back and one with a yellow rounded back, each with a small dark head and short antennae, shown close up so the difference in colour between them is easy to compare.

pages.text: Some ladybugs are orange. Some ladybugs are other colors.
pages.brief: Several ladybugs in colours beyond red and yellow, one orange and others in further shades, each with the same rounded body and small head, placed side by side so the range of ladybug colours can be seen.

pages.text: Some ladybugs have spots.
pages.brief: Ladybugs with spots, their rounded backs dotted with small dark marks, some carrying a few spots and some carrying more, each ladybug shown close up so the spotted pattern across its back is clear.

pages.text: Some ladybugs have stripes.
pages.brief: Ladybugs with stripes, lines running across their rounded backs instead of spots, each stripe standing out clearly on the shell, with one ladybug shown larger and close up so the striped pattern is easy to see.

pages.text: Some ladybugs have just one color.
pages.brief: Ladybugs that are all one colour, their rounded backs plain and even, with no spots and no stripes anywhere on them, shown close up so it is clear that the whole back is a single unbroken colour.

pages.text: Some ladybugs eat other insects. Some ladybugs eat plants.
pages.brief: One ladybug eating a smaller insect held near its mouth, and a second ladybug on a plant eating part of that plant, showing the two different kinds of food that ladybugs take.

pages.text: All ladybugs have wings.
pages.brief: Ladybugs with their wings open, the thin flying wings spread out from under the hard rounded back cases, shown ready to fly so the wings that every ladybug has are clearly visible.

books.title: At the Fair
books.art_why: Fairground rides are real places that exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: You can ride the big wheel.
pages.brief: A tall big wheel stands against the sky at a busy fairground, its round cabins slowly turning. In one cabin a young child leans forward and looks out over the fair, hands on the rail, with tents and lights spread out far below.

pages.text: You can ride the little car.
pages.brief: A small brightly coloured car on a fairground track carries a happy young child, hands on the little steering wheel. The car rolls along a curved rail with painted barriers beside it and other little cars waiting behind on the same track.

pages.text: You can ride the long train.
pages.brief: A long train of linked carriages winds around a fairground corner, carrying children who wave from the open seats. The front engine leads the way past striped awnings, and a young child in the middle carriage smiles and holds the side rail.

pages.text: You can ride the fast cup.
pages.brief: Round spinning cups whirl on a fairground ride, each cup painted in bright colours. A young child sits inside one turning cup, gripping the middle wheel and laughing as the cup spins faster, with other cups circling nearby on the platform.

pages.text: You can ride the painted horse.
pages.brief: A painted wooden carousel horse rises and falls on its pole, bright colours on its mane and saddle. A young child sits astride the horse, holding the pole with both hands, while other painted horses and lights of the carousel turn around them.

pages.text: You can ride the giant swing.
pages.brief: A giant swing ride lifts children high into the air, seats hanging on long chains from a turning top. A young child swings out wide in one seat, feet dangling, with the fairground tents and paths small and far below.

pages.text: You can ride the tiny plane.
pages.brief: A tiny plane ride circles on a fairground platform, small painted planes tipping up and down. A young child sits in one little plane, hands on the controls, smiling as the plane rises slightly above the others on their arms.

pages.text: What is your favorite ride at the fair?
pages.brief: A wide view of the fairground in the evening, with the big wheel, carousel, train and spinning cups all lit up. Children and families walk along the path between the rides, pointing and choosing where to go next.

books.title: Spirals, Spirals Everywhere
books.art_why: The book shows real objects such as a horn, shell, plant, finger, cloud and hair, which can be photographed.

pages.text: A spiral is a shape. A spiral can be found in many things.
pages.brief: A large, clear spiral shape fills the center of a clean, light background, curving inward in smooth loops. The spiral is shown as a simple shape for a young reader to look at, with open space around it so its curve is easy to see.

pages.text: This horn has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of a single horn with a clear spiral curve, resting against a plain neutral background. The horn's ridged surface follows the spiral from the wider base toward the tip, and the whole horn is shown clearly so its spiral shape is easy to see.

pages.text: This shell has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of one seashell with a clear spiral, resting on a plain neutral surface. The shell's curve winds inward from the outer edge toward the center, and the shell is shown large in the frame so its spiral pattern is easy to see.

pages.text: This plant has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of a green plant with a spiral, shown against a soft plain background. A curling stem or leaf winds inward in a clear spiral, and the plant is shown large enough for a young reader to see the spiral curve in its shape.

pages.text: This finger has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of one fingertip with a clear spiral, shown against a soft plain background. The fine lines on the finger curve around in a spiral pattern, and the fingertip fills the frame so the spiral is easy to see.

pages.text: This cloud has a spiral.
pages.brief: A single cloud in a clear sky, shaped with a clear spiral curve. The cloud's soft edges wind inward in a spiral form, and the sky around it is open and plain so the spiral shape stands out clearly.

pages.text: This hair has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of curly hair with a clear spiral, shown against a soft plain background. One curl winds around in a tight spiral, and the hair fills the frame so the spiral shape is easy for a young reader to see.

pages.text: A spiral is a shape. Can you find the spirals?
pages.brief: Several clear spiral shapes are placed across a simple, open scene. Each spiral curls inward in smooth loops, and the view invites a young reader to look carefully and find the spirals in the scene.

books.title: That's a Fruit?
books.art_why: Real fruits exist and can be photographed.

pages.text: All fruits have seeds. Some fruits may surprise you.
pages.brief: A bright assortment of fresh fruits is shown, with several fruits cut open to reveal their seeds. The fruits sit in a simple, clear arrangement that lets young readers look closely at the seeds inside. The scene feels friendly and curious, matching a simple question about surprising fruits.

pages.text: An avocado is a fruit.
pages.brief: A ripe avocado is shown whole and also halved, with its large round pit visible inside the green flesh. The avocado rests in a plain, well-lit setting so its shape and color are easy to see. The view is simple and close, focusing only on the avocado as a surprising fruit.

pages.text: A tomato is a fruit.
pages.brief: A red tomato is shown whole and sliced open to show its juicy inside and small seeds. It sits alone in a clean, bright view, with its smooth skin and round shape clearly visible. The close picture keeps the focus on the tomato as one surprising fruit.

pages.text: A cucumber is a fruit.
pages.brief: A green cucumber is shown whole and cut open, revealing its pale inside and small seeds. It rests in a simple, bright view so its long shape and bumpy skin are easy to see. The close scene focuses only on the cucumber as a surprising fruit.

pages.text: A pepper is a fruit.
pages.brief: A bright pepper is shown whole and cut open, with its shiny skin and seeds visible inside. It sits in a clean, well-lit view so its color and shape stand out clearly. The simple close scene focuses only on the pepper as a surprising fruit.

pages.text: A pumpkin is a fruit.
pages.brief: A large orange pumpkin is shown whole and cut open, with its thick flesh and seeds visible inside. It rests in a plain, bright view so its round shape and ribbed skin are easy to see. The close scene focuses only on the pumpkin as a surprising fruit.

pages.text: An eggplant is a fruit.
pages.brief: A deep purple eggplant is shown whole and cut open, revealing its pale inside and small seeds. It sits in a clean, bright view so its smooth skin and long shape are easy to see. The close scene focuses only on the eggplant as a surprising fruit.

pages.text: Can you name some other surprising fruits?
pages.brief: Several fresh fruits are arranged together in a simple, bright view, with space around them as if waiting for more examples. The scene is open and curious, showing only colorful fruits and no people. The arrangement keeps the focus on the question about other surprising fruits.

books.title: What Animals Eat
books.art_why: Real animals eating are everyday subjects that can be photographed today.

pages.text: Cows like to eat grass. Munch, munch.
pages.brief: A brown and white cow stands in a green grassy field, head down, chewing mouthfuls of grass. Its tail hangs behind it. Soft sunlight falls on the pasture. The cow keeps munching steadily, filling the frame with a calm, everyday farm scene.

pages.text: Crunch, crunch. Birds like to eat seeds.
pages.brief: Several small birds gather on the ground, pecking at scattered seeds. One bird holds a seed in its beak. They stand on dry earth with short grass around them. The birds crunch the seeds as they feed together in the open.

pages.text: Pandas like to eat leaves. Munch, munch.
pages.brief: A giant panda sits among thick green bamboo, holding leafy stalks in its paws. It chews the leaves slowly. The panda's black and white fur stands out against the bamboo. It rests on the ground, surrounded by more bamboo shoots and leaves.

pages.text: Zap, zap. Frogs like to eat bugs.
pages.brief: A green frog sits on wet ground, its long sticky tongue shooting out to catch a small flying bug. The bug is tiny in the air. The frog's eyes are wide and focused. Water and reeds are nearby.

pages.text: Monkeys like to eat fruit. Slurp, slurp.
pages.brief: A monkey sits in a tree, holding a ripe piece of fruit in its hands. Juice drips as it takes a big bite. Leaves and branches surround the monkey. It slurps the sweet fruit, looking relaxed and happy in the warm canopy.

pages.text: Gulp, gulp. Seals like to eat fish.
pages.brief: A seal swims in clear blue water, a silver fish caught in its mouth. It tilts its head back and gulps the fish down. Bubbles rise around its whiskered face. The seal's smooth body glides through the water.

pages.text: Goats like to eat everything. Hey, stop! That’s my sock.
pages.brief: A goat stands in a yard, mouth open, chewing on a brightly coloured sock. The sock stretches from the goat's mouth. The goat looks bold and curious, ready to nibble anything nearby. A simple outdoor setting with grass and a fence behind.

pages.text: That’s my book. Hey, stop! That’s my shoe. Hey, stop!
pages.brief: The same goat now holds a book in its mouth and a shoe nearby. It chews the corner of the book and nudges the shoe with its nose. The goat stands in the same yard, looking pleased with its stolen treasures. Grass and a fence are behind it.

books.title: Strange Animals
books.art_why: Strange animals exist today, so photographs are appropriate.

pages.text: Animals are living things. Some animals look strange.
pages.brief: A natural outdoor scene shows several different living animals together, some with odd shapes and features. They are clearly alive and moving in a simple setting that helps show animals are living things and some look strange.

pages.text: A panda ant looks strange.
pages.brief: A panda ant is shown alone in clear close-up against a simple background. Its unusual body shape and markings are easy to see, making its strange appearance the main focus of the picture for young readers.

pages.text: A blue dragon looks strange.
pages.brief: A blue dragon is shown alone in clear close-up against a simple background. Its unusual body shape and colours are easy to see, making its strange appearance the main focus of the picture for young readers.

pages.text: A star spider looks strange.
pages.brief: A star spider is shown alone in clear close-up against a simple background. Its unusual body shape and markings are easy to see, making its strange appearance the main focus of the picture for young readers.

pages.text: A turtle frog looks strange.
pages.brief: A turtle frog is shown alone in clear close-up against a simple background. Its unusual body shape and features are easy to see, making its strange appearance the main focus of the picture for young readers.

pages.text: A rosy moth looks strange.
pages.brief: A rosy moth is shown alone in clear close-up against a simple background. Its unusual body shape and colours are easy to see, making its strange appearance the main focus of the picture for young readers.

pages.text: A water bear looks strange.
pages.brief: A water bear is shown alone in clear close-up against a simple background. Its unusual body shape and features are easy to see, making its strange appearance the main focus of the picture for young readers.

pages.text: Do these animals look strange?
pages.brief: The strange animals shown before are gathered together in a simple outdoor display, each shown clearly. Their different shapes and features are easy to compare, inviting the reader to decide whether these animals look strange.

books.title: Ice
books.art_why: Ice is a real-world weather and nature subject that can be photographed.

pages.text: Ice forms when water gets cold and freezes.
pages.brief: A close view of water in cold air, its surface turning hard and glassy as it freezes into ice. The water and the new ice fill the frame in a cold, simple outdoor setting, showing the moment water becomes solid ice.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet house.
pages.brief: A wet house outside on a cold day, with a thin layer of ice forming on its wet wall and roofline. The house stands in the cold air, and the icy patch clings to the wet surface, showing ice forming on a wet house.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet fence.
pages.brief: A wet wooden fence outdoors in cold weather, with ice forming along its wet rails and posts. The fence stands in the cold air, and clear icy patches cling to the wet wood, showing ice forming on a wet fence.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet car.
pages.brief: A wet car parked outdoors in cold weather, with ice forming on its wet windows, hood and doors. The car sits in the cold air, and a thin icy layer clings to the wet surfaces, showing ice forming on a wet car.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet road.
pages.brief: A wet road outdoors in cold weather, with ice forming across the wet surface. The road stretches through the cold scene, and a thin, glassy icy layer covers parts of the wet pavement, showing ice forming on a wet road.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet sign.
pages.brief: A wet sign outdoors in cold weather, with ice forming on its wet face and edges. The sign stands in the cold air, and clear icy patches cling to the wet surface, showing ice forming on a wet sign.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet sidewalk.
pages.brief: A wet sidewalk outdoors in cold weather, with ice forming along the wet pavement. The sidewalk stretches through the cold scene, and a thin, glassy icy layer covers parts of the wet concrete, showing ice forming on a wet sidewalk.

pages.text: Ice can be very slippery!
pages.brief: A close view of smooth ice outdoors, its surface shiny and glassy in the cold air. The ice fills the frame with a slick, hard sheen, showing that ice can be very slippery underfoot.

books.title: Animals That Sting
books.art_why: Real animals such as bees, jellyfish, worms, rays, ants and wasps can be photographed.

pages.text: Some animals sting to defend themselves. Stings can hurt.
pages.brief: Several different animals that can sting are shown together in a simple natural setting, each in a defensive pose. The picture introduces the idea that some animals sting to defend themselves and that stings can hurt.

pages.text: This bee stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A single bee is shown close up in a natural setting, stinging to defend itself. Its striped body and stinger are clear, and the picture focuses on the bee and its defensive action. No other animals or people appear.

pages.text: This jellyfish stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A single jellyfish is shown close up in the water, stinging to defend itself. Its soft body and trailing tentacles are clear as it carries out this defensive action. The picture focuses only on the jellyfish.

pages.text: This worm stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A single worm is shown close up, stinging to defend itself. Its long, soft body is clear, and the picture focuses on the worm and its defensive action. No other animals or people appear.

pages.text: This ray stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A single ray is shown close up in the water, stinging to defend itself. Its flat body and tail are clear as it carries out this defensive action, and the picture focuses only on the ray.

pages.text: This ant stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A single ant is shown close up, stinging to defend itself. Its small body and stinger are clear, and the picture focuses on the ant and its defensive action in a simple natural setting. No other animals or people appear.

pages.text: This wasp stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A single wasp is shown close up, stinging to defend itself. Its narrow body and stinger are clear, and the picture focuses on the wasp and its defensive action in a simple natural setting. No other animals or people appear.

pages.text: Stings can help keep animals safe.
pages.brief: Several animals that sting are shown together in a simple natural setting. The picture focuses on how stings can help keep animals safe, with the animals in defensive poses and no people or extra objects.

books.title: Airplanes
books.art_why: Airplanes are real machines that exist today and are photographed every day.

pages.text: Airplanes are amazing machines.
pages.brief: A large silver passenger airplane stands on an airport runway in bright daylight, its wings spread wide and engines gleaming. Its nose points down the long grey strip of runway, ready to roll forward, with open sky and a few distant clouds behind it.

pages.text: People use airplanes to get things.
pages.brief: A big cargo airplane sits on the tarmac with its side door open. Workers in bright vests load stacked cardboard boxes and parcels up a ramp into the hold, while a small loader vehicle waits nearby carrying more boxes to go inside the plane.

pages.text: People use airplanes to go places.
pages.brief: Families with rolling suitcases and backpacks walk across the airport apron toward a waiting airplane, climbing the stairs to the door. A parent holds a child's hand, and other passengers queue behind them under the open sky beside the plane's wing.

pages.text: People use airplanes to put out fires.
pages.brief: A firefighting airplane flies low over a hillside, releasing a thick cloud of red water that falls toward smoking trees below. Grey smoke rises from the burning brush while the plane's belly tanks empty out over the slope.

pages.text: People use airplanes to help grow food.
pages.brief: A small yellow crop-dusting airplane flies very low over a wide green farm field, spraying a fine mist behind it. Rows of young crops stretch to the horizon, and a farmer on a tractor watches from the edge of the field.

pages.text: People use airplanes to do tricks.
pages.brief: A bright aerobatic airplane loops upside down high in a clear blue sky, leaving a long white smoke trail curling behind it. Below, a crowd of people stands on an airfield looking up at the spinning plane overhead.

pages.text: People use airplanes to have fun.
pages.brief: A small light airplane with a smiling pilot lifts off a grassy airfield while a family on the ground waves and points. A child jumps with excitement, and picnic blankets and a cooler sit nearby on the grass in the sunshine.

pages.text: People use airplanes in many ways.
pages.brief: Many different airplanes are shown together at a busy airport: a big jet at a gate, a cargo plane being loaded, a small yellow crop duster and a bright aerobatic plane. Ground crew walk between them across the wide concrete apron.

books.title: What Does the Wind Move?
books.art_why: Wind, sailboats, balloons, windmills and kites are real things a camera can capture today.

pages.text: The wind moves many things.
pages.brief: A wide outdoor view on a breezy day, showing leaves and grass bending as the wind passes over them, with a few everyday things like a kite and a sail visible far off in the distance, all of them gently stirred by the moving air.

pages.text: The wind pushes a sailboat.
pages.brief: A small sailboat on open water with its white sail filled and curved by the wind, the boat leaning slightly as it moves forward across the rippled surface, with open sky and a stretch of water behind it and no people in the scene.

pages.text: The wind carries a balloon.
pages.brief: A bright balloon drifting through the open air above a grassy field, tilted and pushed along by the wind, with soft clouds and blue sky behind it and the ground far below, showing the air carrying it away.

pages.text: The wind floats a bag.
pages.brief: A light plastic bag floating and tumbling in the air above a pavement on a windy day, lifted and carried along by the breeze, with a simple outdoor background of sky, a wall and a few blurred branches behind it.

pages.text: The wind turns a windmill.
pages.brief: A tall windmill standing in an open field with its large blades caught by the wind and turning, the sails angled against a breezy sky, with grass and a few small plants around its base and nothing else in the frame.

pages.text: The wind lifts a kite.
pages.brief: A kite rising high in the sky on a gusty day, its tail streaming and fluttering as the wind lifts it upward, with open blue sky and soft clouds around it and green ground far below.

pages.text: The wind blows a shirt.
pages.brief: A shirt hanging on an outdoor line, puffed out and flapping as the wind blows through it, with the line stretched between two posts, grass beneath and a plain breezy sky behind, nobody in the picture.

pages.text: It is always moving something! The wind moves many things.
pages.brief: A breezy outdoor scene with several things moving at once: a kite high up, a balloon drifting, a sailboat's sail far off on the water and a windmill turning, grass and leaves bending, all stirred by the same wind under a cloudy sky.

books.title: So Many Fish
books.art_why: Fish are real animals that exist today, so photographs suit the book.

pages.text: This fish is silver and shiny.
pages.brief: A single fish with bright silver scales swims in the water. Its body shines and catches the light, and its fins spread out as it moves forward. The fish looks smooth and gleaming, with a clear eye and a graceful tail.

pages.text: This fish is blue and bright.
pages.brief: A blue fish glides through the water, its bright colour standing out clearly. Its scales look vivid and clean, and its fins are open as it swims along. The fish faces forward, calm and colourful, with a shining tail behind it.

pages.text: This fish is red and scary.
pages.brief: A red fish faces forward in the water, looking scary with a fierce expression. Its mouth is wide, its fins are sharp, and its bright red body makes it stand out. The fish seems bold and alarming as it swims, with a strong, warning look.

pages.text: This fish is brown and pointy.
pages.brief: A brown fish swims in the water with a pointy shape. Sharp fins and a narrow, pointed body give it a spiky look. Its brown scales are dull but clear, and its tail comes to a point as it moves forward, looking prickly and tough.

pages.text: This fish is black and spotted.
pages.brief: A black fish swims in the water, covered in clear spots. Its dark body is dotted with lighter marks, and its fins spread out on both sides. The spotted fish looks striking as it moves along, with a rounded tail and a steady, calm gaze.

pages.text: This fish is yellow and boxy.
pages.brief: A yellow fish swims in the water with a boxy, square shape. Its body looks firm and blocky, with flat sides and neat fins. The bright yellow colour makes it easy to see as it moves forward, solid and sturdy in the water.

pages.text: This fish is orange and striped.
pages.brief: An orange fish swims in the water with clear stripes across its body. The stripes run along its sides, and its fins are spread as it moves. Bright orange and patterned, the fish looks lively and neat, with a rounded tail behind it.

pages.text: This fish is gold and puffy.
pages.brief: A gold fish swims in the water, its body puffed up and round. The shining gold colour makes it gleam, and its small fins stick out from the puffy shape. It looks full and swollen as it floats along, bright and smooth.

pages.text: This fish is purple and fancy.
pages.brief: A purple fish swims in the water with a fancy look. Its fins are long and flowing, spreading out like decorations around its body. The rich purple colour and elegant shape make it stand out as it moves, graceful and showy.

pages.text: So many fish swim in the sea!
pages.brief: Many fish swim together in the sea. Silver, blue, red, brown, black, yellow, orange, gold and purple fish fill the water, moving in different directions. The whole group is colourful and busy, swimming through the open sea.

books.title: Tools
books.art_why: Real tools that exist today are best shown in clear photographs.

pages.text: I see tools everywhere. Tools help us work.
pages.brief: A young child stands in a busy workspace and looks around at many simple tools resting on shelves, hooks and a low bench. The tools are ready for work, showing that tools can be found in many places and help people do jobs.

pages.text: It is a pencil for writing. Here is a tool.
pages.brief: A close view of a child’s hand holding a pencil, the point pressed to a plain sheet while the pencil moves to write. The pencil is shown clearly as a useful writing tool, simple and easy to see.

pages.text: Here is a tool. It is a rake for raking.
pages.brief: A rake with a long handle and metal tines is held outdoors, its head resting on the ground. It is being used to rake, with the tines pulling across the surface in a clear, simple view of this tool at work.

pages.text: It is a hammer for pounding. Here is a tool.
pages.brief: A hammer with a solid head and handle is held firmly and swung down to pound. The hammer is the focus, shown in a simple work setting with the head striking downward, making clear what this tool is used for.

pages.text: Here is a tool. It is a shovel for digging.
pages.brief: A shovel with a long handle and broad blade is pushed into the ground to dig. The blade cuts into soil while the handle is gripped, showing the shovel clearly as a tool for digging in a simple outdoor scene.

pages.text: It is a knife for cutting. Here is a tool.
pages.brief: A knife with a handle and sharp blade is held firmly, the edge ready to cut. The knife is shown close and clear, with the blade angled toward a simple surface, making the cutting tool easy to see.

pages.text: Here is a tool. It is a wheelbarrow for carrying.
pages.brief: A wheelbarrow with a tray, two handles and a single front wheel is held and pushed along the ground. It is shown being used to carry, with the wheelbarrow clear and simple in an outdoor setting as a tool for carrying loads.

pages.text: What tools do you see? I see tools everywhere.
pages.brief: A young child stands with arms open wide, looking at tools all around: a pencil, rake, hammer, shovel, knife and wheelbarrow. The tools are placed across the scene, showing that tools can be seen everywhere.

books.title: The Animals of Canada
books.art_why: All these animals exist today and can be photographed in Canada.

pages.text: This is a moose. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: A large moose stands in a Canadian wetland, its broad antlers spread wide above its long head. Its dark brown coat and long legs are clearly visible as it stands among low green bushes beside calm water, with tall evergreen trees in the background under a soft sky.

pages.text: It lives in Canada. This is a goose.
pages.brief: A Canada goose stands at the edge of a pond in Canada, its black neck and white cheek patch clearly shown. Its grey-brown body and webbed feet rest on the grassy bank, and calm water with green reeds stretches behind the bird under an open sky.

pages.text: This is a bear. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: A bear walks through a Canadian forest, its thick fur and heavy body filling the frame. The bear moves between tall evergreen trees and rocks, with green undergrowth around its paws and soft daylight falling through the branches above the woodland floor.

pages.text: It lives in Canada. This is a beaver.
pages.brief: A beaver sits at the edge of a river in Canada, its dark brown fur and flat tail visible. The beaver rests on the muddy bank beside still water, with cut branches and green shrubs nearby, and a quiet line of trees stands along the far shore.

pages.text: This is an eagle. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: An eagle perches on a thick branch in Canada, its dark feathers and pale head clearly visible. The bird's sharp curved beak and strong talons grip the wood as it looks out over a wide landscape of green trees and open sky behind it.

pages.text: It lives in Canada. This is a wolf.
pages.brief: A wolf stands in a snowy Canadian woodland, its grey coat and pointed ears clear against the pale ground. The wolf faces forward between bare trunks and low snow-covered bushes, with soft winter light and a quiet line of trees fading into the distance.

pages.text: This is a loon. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: A loon floats on a calm Canadian lake, its black and white patterned feathers and sharp beak clearly shown. The bird rests low on the still water, with a soft reflection beneath it and a dark green shoreline of trees far behind.

pages.text: Many animals live in Canada.
pages.brief: Many Canadian animals share a wide landscape: a moose, a goose, a bear, a beaver, an eagle, a wolf and a loon are all shown across the scene. Forest, water and open sky spread behind them as the animals stand and rest in their Canadian home.

books.title: Rocks
books.art_why: Rocks, mountains, boulders and sand are real things that photograph clearly.

pages.text: This is a mountain.
pages.brief: A tall rocky mountain rising against the sky, grey stone slopes with a few patches of green low down, wide view from a distance so the whole mountain shape is clear.

pages.text: A mountain is made of rock.
pages.brief: Close view of the mountain's surface: solid grey rock in rough layers, cracked and weathered, filling the picture so the stone the mountain is made of is easy to see.

pages.text: This is a boulder. It broke off the mountain.
pages.brief: A big rounded boulder lying on the ground at the foot of the mountain slope, broken away from the rock face above it, with smaller loose pieces of stone scattered around it.

pages.text: This is a stone. It broke off the boulder.
pages.brief: A hand-sized stone resting on the ground beside the large boulder, its edges rough where it split away, with the boulder's shadow falling across the dry ground behind it.

pages.text: This is a pebble. It broke off the stone.
pages.brief: A small pebble held between two fingers, smooth and grey, with the stone it came from lying on the ground below and out of focus behind it.

pages.text: This is sand. It broke off the pebble.
pages.brief: A close view of coarse sand grains on the ground, tiny separate pieces in tan and grey, heaped in a small pile near the pebble on dry earth.

pages.text: This is dust.
pages.brief: An extremely close view of fine dust powder on a flat surface, pale grey specks settled in a thin layer, with a little of it lifted into the air.

pages.text: Dust is the tiniest piece of rock. Dust is everywhere.
pages.brief: Dust specks floating in a shaft of sunlight indoors and settled as a fine film on a wooden shelf and windowsill, showing dust in the air and on surfaces.

books.title: Making Salsa!
books.art_why: Salsa ingredients and cooking are real-world subjects.

pages.text: In go the peppers.
pages.brief: A close view of peppers as they go down into a bowl for salsa. The peppers are the main subject, shown whole and easy to see, with the page focused only on the peppers being added and the simple downward motion of putting them in.

pages.text: In goes the onion.
pages.brief: A close view of an onion as it goes down into the salsa bowl. The onion is the only ingredient in focus, shown whole and clear, and the page shows the simple action of the onion being placed into the bowl for salsa making.

pages.text: In goes the tomato.
pages.brief: A close view of a tomato as it goes down into the salsa bowl. The tomato is the only ingredient in focus, shown whole and clear, and the page shows the simple action of the tomato being placed into the bowl for salsa making.

pages.text: In goes the salt.
pages.brief: A close view of salt as it goes down into the salsa bowl. The salt is shown as a small pour or sprinkle, the only ingredient in focus, and the page shows the simple action of salt being added into the bowl for the salsa.

pages.text: In goes the black pepper.
pages.brief: A close view of black pepper as it goes down into the salsa bowl. The black pepper is shown as a small sprinkle, the only ingredient in focus, and the page shows the simple action of black pepper being added into the bowl for the salsa.

pages.text: In goes the cilantro.
pages.brief: A close view of cilantro as it goes down into the salsa bowl. The cilantro is the only ingredient in focus, shown leafy and clear, and the page shows the simple action of cilantro being placed into the bowl for salsa making.

pages.text: In goes the lemon juice.
pages.brief: A close view of lemon juice as it goes down into the salsa bowl. The lemon juice is shown as a pour, the only ingredient in focus, and the page shows the simple action of lemon juice being added into the bowl for the salsa.

pages.text: We eat chips and salsa! I mix the salsa.
pages.brief: A child is mixing the salsa in a bowl while other people at the table eat chips and salsa. The child’s hands and the bowl are in clear view, and the group is eating chips with the salsa they have made.
